To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phagocytic defect in leukocyte adhesion-deficiency neutrophils can be reproduced in healthy neutrophils by anti-CD11/CD18 monoclonal antibodies.
the CD11b/ CD18-dependent and - independent mechanisms of ingestion are distinct and that anti-CD11/CD18 MABs inhibit both mechanisms of ingestion.
the CD11b/ CD18-dependent mechanism of ingestion is mediated by PKC, and CD11b/18-independent ingestion is mediated by cAMP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of phagocyte function and their modulation by inflammatory mediators.
the mechanisms by which inflammatory mediators augment phagocytic activity in normal PMN and with the mechanisms by whicb CD11b/ CD18 deficiency results in the LAD phenotype.
the molecular and biochemical basis for the phagocytic defect of LAD PMN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD11b/ CD18-dependent mechanism of phagocytic ingestion involves PKC and cAMP, whereas the CD11b-dependent mechanism of ingestion involves only cAMP.
CD11b is a receptor for phagocytotic ingestion, but CD11a, CD18, and CD11c do not have such a role.
CD11/CD 18-deficient PMNs exhibit a specific defect in phagocytic amplification, but retain the ability to phagocytize by a CD11b/ CD18-independent mechanism, which is cAMP-dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LAD PMNs are defective in phagocytotic function because they are unable to amplify phagocyte function in response to inflammatory mediators.
LAD PMNs have a specific and profound defect in PKC-mediated phagocytotic responses, which can be mimicked in normal PMN with anti-CD11/CD18 MAAbs.
the CD11b/18 complex is required for both the CD11b-dependent and -indefendent pathways of phagocytic stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is more than one pathway of phagocytic ingestion and that CD11b is a major player in the PKC-mediated pathway of phagocyte ingestion.
there is more than one mechanism for phagocytosing particles, and that the mechanism that is used is determined by the particle and the type of phagocyte.
CD11b-dependent and -indepdendent mechanisms exist for phagocytosing particles and that the CD11b-dependent mechanism may be mediated by a protein kinase A-dependent pathway.
